questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

My mother said that the police had been patrolling the previous night.
options_en: My mother said, "The police have been patrolled the last night."
My mother said, "The police is patrolling the last night."
My mother said, "The police patrolled the last night."
My mother said, "The police were patrolling the last night."
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Direct Speech will be in Past Continuous Tense.

Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had been + V1 + ing + Object) will be converted into Past Continuous (Subject + was/were+V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said that he had been watching television the previous night. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I was watching television last night" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect speech to Direct Speech:
Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
Said thatsaid
had been patrollingwere patrolling
Previous nightLast night

From the given options, the sentence that follows the above mentioned conditions for Direct speech is option (d) "My mother said, "The police were patrolling the last night.""

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

NOTE:

V1 -> Base form/simple form of verb, V2 -> Past form of verb (-ed form or irregular verb), V3 -> Past participle form of verb (-ed, -d, -t, -en, or -n), V4 -> Continuous form of verb / Present participle form of verb (-ing form), V5 -> Third person singular (V1+ -es or -s).

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The boy, as well as / his friends, were / absent from the class / when the teacher came.
questions.solution_en:
When words like along with, together with, as well as, accompanied by etc. are used to combine two subjects, the verb agrees with the subject mentioned first.

So, the verb 'were' (plural) does not agree with the first subject 'the boy' (singular). It should be replaced with the singular verb 'was'.

So, there is an error in part in option (c).

The correct sentence is: The boy, as well as his friends, was absent from the class when the teacher came.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

Supposing that the doctor tells us to come soon, we will book our flights immediately.
questions.solution_en:
The use of 'supposing if' is grammatically incorrect because 'supposing' and 'if' carry the same meaning. The conjunction 'that' is used with 'Supposing'.

For example: Supposing that it rains, you will get wet.

Thus, options (a) and (c) are incorrect.

The tense in the 'Supposing that' clause should be in the Simple Present Tense (tells) when the tense in the main clause is in the Simple Future Tense denoted by a modal verb (will). Thus, option (b) is incorrect.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (d) No improvement required .

Additional Information:

You use 'suppose' or 'supposing' when you are considering a possible situation or action and trying to think what effects it would have.

'Supposing' can be used independently also (without the use of 'that').

For example: He was bluffed into supposing I was ill-prepared.
